verdict.rationale: Superpowers documents automatic, context-driven skill activation. The README says skills trigger automatically. A session-start bootstrap tells the agent it has skills and must invoke relevant ones before any action, and the using-superpowers skill routes tasks to skills (e.g. "Fix this bug" goes to systematic-debugging). Skills are written TDD-style with pressure scenarios, and an eval harness judges skill compliance on real Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI sessions. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of how the description/frontmatter text is tuned to drive trigger selection, and independent or hands-on corroboration that the right skill actually fires at the right moment (the runtime probe only verified installation).

support.subject: As a developer, installed skills trigger automatically from task context, with descriptions engineered so the agent activates the right skill at the right moment

citations.quote: because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.
Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files.

You write test cases (pressure scenarios with subagents), watch them fail (baseline behavior), write the skill (documentation), watch tests pass (agents comply), and refactor (close loopholes).
Python harness driving real tmux sessions of Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI, with an LLM actor and verifier judging skill compliance.
so that Superpowers skills auto-trigger there the same way they do natively.
